ui.scope: Authored local scenarios. No real cluster, network, scheduler or controller is run. Repairs affect only this lesson.
ui.evidence: Inspect the listed evidence before applying a repair.
ui.fixed: The local repair has been applied. Inspect the resulting state before continuing.
ui.observe: Inspect the resulting Pod or endpoints in Properties.
ui.evidenceError: Some required evidence has not been inspected. Open the listed object views first.
ui.diagnosisError: The selected explanation does not match the observations. Recheck the evidence.
ui.repairError: That change does not resolve the observed cause. Compare its field and value with the evidence.
ui.complete: You diagnosed and repaired both new cases without hints.
ui.noEvents: No events in this authored snapshot.
ui.noLogs: No container logs are available in this snapshot. The container may not have started.
ui.noSecrets: Secret values are never included. Only reference names and key names are shown.
ui.memory: Progress lasts while this library is open. Closing it clears lesson state.
ui.observations: Given scenario observations · not Kubernetes API fields

diagnoses.selector: The Service selector does not match the application Pod labels.
diagnoses.port: The Service forwards to a different port from the application listener.
diagnoses.readiness: The readiness probe checks a path that the application does not serve.
diagnoses.startup: Liveness restarts the container before slow initialization can finish.
diagnoses.image: The requested image tag is absent from the supplied image catalogue.
diagnoses.command: The application exits because its arguments are invalid.
diagnoses.environment: The environment value was captured before the ConfigMap changed.
diagnoses.secret: The required Secret key name does not exist.
diagnoses.requests: The CPU request does not fit the remaining request budget.
diagnoses.memory: The container exceeded its memory limit; the recorded reason is OOMKilled.
diagnoses.credentials: The image registry requires different credentials.
diagnoses.usage: Low observed CPU usage means any CPU request will fit.
diagnoses.replicas: More replicas alone will repair this configuration.

selector.goal: Restore traffic without changing the application. Compare Service, Pod and EndpointSlice.
selector.hint: Compare spec.selector with metadata.labels; an empty ready endpoint set needs an explanation.
selector.why: Matching the intended Pod labels supplies backends; a Service does not create Pods.

port.goal: Restore traffic when ready backends already exist. Check both Service ports and the listener.
port.hint: A ready address alone is not enough: compare targetPort with the application port.
port.why: targetPort is the backend port. A ready endpoint does not prove end-to-end reachability.

readiness.goal: Make a running application ready for Service traffic without adding restarts.
readiness.hint: Compare the readiness HTTP path with logs. The live endpoint and readiness endpoint serve different checks.
readiness.why: Readiness controls normal Service eligibility; a failed readiness check alone does not restart a container.

startup.goal: Allow the documented slow initialization while retaining liveness protection.
startup.hint: Compare initialization time with the probe window. A startup probe delays liveness and readiness until it succeeds.
startup.why: The authored startup budget covers the observed cold start. It is not a universal probe configuration.

image.goal: Start the application using an image present in the supplied catalogue.
image.hint: Read the pull failure reason and the approved tag. Do not invent logs for a container that never started.
image.why: A missing manifest is addressed by the reviewed image reference, not by repeatedly pulling the same missing tag.

command.goal: Find why a pulled image still exits and fix the application launch arguments.
command.hint: Compare previous-container logs with the workload arguments. CrashLoopBackOff is a symptom, not a root cause.
command.why: The observed exit was caused by an invalid option. Restarting unchanged arguments would repeat that failure.

environment.goal: Use the current ConfigMap value in the application environment. Compare the reference and the running snapshot.
environment.hint: An existing process keeps its captured environment. A reviewed template change creates a new container in this scenario.
environment.why: ConfigMap environment values require new containers. Mounted-file updates and application reloads are different mechanisms.

secret.goal: Resolve the required Secret reference without reading or inventing a Secret value.
secret.hint: Compare secretKeyRef.key with the listed key names and the startup event. Making the reference optional does not supply the required value.
secret.why: The corrected reference uses an existing key. Key names do not reveal the Secret value or prove that access is authorized.

requests.goal: Schedule the workload using its supplied validated CPU request, without overcommitting the request budget.
requests.hint: Compare allocatable minus already allocated requests with this request. Current CPU use is not that budget.
requests.why: The validated request fits the given remaining budget. A higher CPU limit alone cannot make an oversized request schedulable.

memory.goal: Resolve the recorded OOMKilled condition within the supplied approved memory budget.
memory.hint: Compare the recorded termination reason, workload limit, validated working set and remaining node budget.
memory.why: The scoped limit change accommodates the documented working set. Exit code alone would not prove OOMKilled; memory requirements are workload-specific.
